approach: Add one reading check, `check_records_measure`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs` beside `check_history_fixture`. It has the same gate (`changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, surveys.rs:237). It fires on either of two triggers. (a) WORDS: the summary or a criterion names a records-computed measure by its real names: keep rule, planning cost, refusal rate(s), refusal count(s), refusal share, check duration(s), landing time(s), landed time, time spent, wasted work, and throughput only in records phrases (throughput section, review, figure(s), measure(s), status). Matching is whole words on lowercase, whitespace-normalised text with hyphens and underscores read as spaces. (b) PATHS: a non-deleted deliverable is a measure-only module, located by reading the code: `crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs`, `crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs` and `crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs` (its module doc, lines 1-2, says it holds planning cost, the keep rule, later harm and producer settings; `keep_rule` is at planning.rs:242, `planning_cost` at :304). The per-rule refusal counts (`ReadingRuleStats`, status.rs:185) live in the shared status.rs, so `status.rs` is not a path trigger and that measure is caught by words only. A reading that fires is accepted only if one Behavior criterion names `real records`, an independent source (`git log`, `history.json`, `commit times`, `recorded check durations`, `recorded durations`, `landing record timestamps`) and `expected range`. Otherwise the check bails, naming the trigger (word or path) and the missing parts. Criteria that declare the replay share (they contain `newly refused`) are not scanned for words, and the sentence `higher refusal rate is intended` is stripped after whitespace normalisation. The refusal text's example takes the expected range from `history.json` commit times or landing record timestamps and presents `status --snapshot` only as the real output checked against that range. The step is one `step!` line in `refusing_check` after `check_history_fixture`. One reader rule line and one planner rule line state the rule. The reader section does not grow, because existing lines are shortened by the new line's length.

decisions.choice: Trigger on measure-only module paths as well as on words, and widen the word list from the measures' real names (finding 5). Paths: crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs, crates/athena-core/src/status/planning.rs (non-deleted deliverables only). Words add refusal count(s), refusal share, landed time, time spent, wasted work. Bare 'throughput' narrows to throughput section/review/figure(s)/measure(s)/status.
decisions.reason: HISTORY.txt shows the keyword list alone misses real measure changes: line 109 (5724053, 'refusal counts'), line 441 ('wasted work', 'landed time'), line 1233 ('time spent'), and lines 86-99 (3a25c33 touched records/throughput.rs under a subject naming no measure). The three modules hold only measure code (status/planning.rs:1-2; status/throughput.rs functions landed_jobs, time_spent, Throughput::compute; records/throughput.rs check_durations). A path trigger there flags no unrelated edit. status.rs is shared with unrelated code, so it is NOT a path trigger and refusal counts are caught by words only; the limit is stated in the doc comment. Narrowing bare 'throughput' stops matches on CI or drain throughput readings. The cost is that a trivial edit to a measure-only module also needs one criterion, which is the intent: both 2026-10-29 landing-time errors came from small changes in such a module.

rejected.why: Misses 5724053, ad7e260-style wording and 3a25c33, shown by HISTORY.txt.

rejected.option: Path trigger on status.rs or all of status/
rejected.why: status.rs and status/ hold unrelated code; it would refuse refactors that move no figure.
Matches readings about CI or drain throughput that compute nothing from records.

decisions.choice: Keep four files outside the reading's deliverable list and say why (findings 1-4): crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs, crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs.
decisions.reason: Each is the only place the behavior lives. checks.rs holds `refusing_check` (checks.rs:518) and its `step!` macro (checks.rs:525); its doc at checks.rs:513-514 says a new check is added as one `step!` line there, never as a direct call, and the file already has `use super::*` (checks.rs:3) so the new function needs no import edit. refusal_corpus.rs must gain a refusing case for the new step line, or `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails and `cargo test` with it. briefs.rs only declares `mod planner; mod reader;` and holds the tests; the rule text is built in briefs/reader.rs (READING_RULES) and briefs/planner.rs (Report string). Nothing else outside the listed deliverables is touched, and no governance file is touched.

rejected.why: It hides a second rule in a function named for another; the corpus step extractor would not see it as its own check, and the history-fixture step-line test would be confused.

rejected.why: They would not reach the generated briefs.

decisions.choice: Do not raise the reader section limit. Keep `assert!(section.len() < 3150)`. The new reader line is at most 220 characters including `- `; existing READING_RULES entries are shortened by at least its length plus 3 bytes, keeping every phrase the tests pin. The producer prints the baseline `section.len()` first, records baseline and new size in the test comment, and asserts the section is no longer than the baseline.
decisions.reason: The reading says the reader line must replace or shorten existing wording; the accepted brief has 2 tokens of reader headroom. If the section cannot fit without losing a rule, the producer stops and reports instead of raising the limit.

rejected.option: Raise the limit to the new size plus a margin
rejected.why: The size test would pass without meeting the criterion.
Many tests pin its phrases and it carries the guidance the checks rely on.

decisions.choice: Fixed planner bound: `REAL_RECORDS_RULE` is one line of at most 200 bytes; a new test finds it exactly once in the Report section and asserts `report.len() <= REPORT_BASE + REAL_RECORDS_RULE.len() + 4`, with REPORT_BASE measured with empty inputs before the change.
decisions.reason: 200 bytes is about 67 tokens, within the planner's 95 tokens of headroom, and later growth fails the test.

decisions.choice: Replay-declaration handling: a criterion whose normalised text contains `newly refused` is skipped for word triggers; elsewhere the sentence `higher refusal rate is intended` is removed after lowercasing and whitespace-normalising, so a wrapped sentence is removed too.
decisions.reason: The reader brief tells readers to write that declaration for every refusal rule; the declaration must not trip another rule. Existing corpus line 2910 and the declared-intended tests (refusal_corpus.rs:2806, 2852, 2947) carry it.

rejected.option: Remove only the literal sentence from raw text

decisions.choice: Independent sources accepted: git log, history.json, commit times, recorded check durations, recorded durations, landing record timestamps. The refusal text and CHANGELOG example take the range from `history.json` commit times or landing record timestamps; `status --snapshot` appears only as the real output that is checked against that range (finding 7).
decisions.reason: `status --snapshot` prints the throughput section (briefs.rs:665-666), which is the output of the code under change, so it cannot be the independent source. The verifier has the evidence snapshot, not git. `git log` is in ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES (surveys.rs:561-567) and needs an `Environment:` assumption. `history.json` and `commit times` are not in that list, and scan_segments breaks a token with an interior `.`, so the history.json form needs no assumption (finding 9); the test asserts it.

rejected.option: Accept only git log and recorded check durations
rejected.why: Forces an Environment assumption and the verifier has no git.

decisions.choice: A code reading that names a measure only to say it is unchanged is refused; a corpus case pins this.
decisions.reason: The check is lexical, as check_history_fixture says (surveys.rs:320-321). A nearby change can still move the figure, which is how both 2026-10-29 landing-time figures went wrong. The cost is one criterion; the doc comment states the limit. HISTORY.txt subjects naming these measures: lines 109, 441, 709, 1233, 1266, 1285, 1400, plus 3a25c33 by path: roughly 8 of 200, so the declared 3% is an estimate; the replay at verification measures the real share.

rejected.why: Needs negation parsing and reopens the gap.

decisions.choice: Satisfy the rule only with one Behavior criterion holding `real records`, an independent source and `expected range`.
decisions.reason: One criterion ties the real run to the independent range; a Content criterion runs nothing.

rejected.why: A real-records criterion could have no range.

decisions.choice: Stored readings that newly fail leave the drain queue (finding 6): intended, and covered by a check_reading_text test.
decisions.reason: drain.rs:114-124 and steward.rs:424 route a stored reading by `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54), which calls `check_reading_acceptance`. A queued measure request (such as one from the throughput review, HISTORY.txt line 709) whose stored reading lacks the criterion stops being run by the batch and waits for `athena go` or a re-read. It is not lost. That is the rule drain already applies to any reading that fails any check, and the existing test drain.rs:4406-4459 pins the mechanism with a stored reading failing a check, so the new check needs no new drain test. A reading.rs test calls `check_reading_text` on a stored measure reading and asserts `ReadingCheck::Refuse` naming the criterion, which is the exact function drain, plan and the steward call.

rejected.why: It would re-test the generic drain routing already pinned at drain.rs:4406; the new part is the Refuse from check_reading_text.
